title: The Dog and Cooking Fairy
text: And so, we ended up going to Cal Mira Island for fun! Well, since there wasn't much need for leveling up this time, we figured a shorter stay would do just fine, so the plan called for fewer days than our previous loops. According to Father, this trip leaned heavily toward being a morale-boosting getaway aimed at helping Itsuki recover mentally.

Also, the plan was to negotiate long-term use of rooms with the Cal Mira side, on the condition that we keep helping revitalize the island. If things went well, the talk was that Big Sister's village folks would get a boost too, indeed. As for personnel, after some discussion, Father decided to bring along his three slaves, Mole, and Panda and the others. Panda, freed from her foster father and grandfather who'd declined to come along, apparently intended to make the most of it. Itsuki brought Riska and Mole and the rest. I'm not sure how Rafumi managed to talk him into it, but apparently Ren was coming too, along with Keel and Luna-chan and the rest of their group. Though, headcount-wise, he was technically coming under Father's party.

Apparently, if Ren left the country for an extended stretch right now, there were concerns about a decline in public order, so the whole thing had to be kept hush-hush. Rafumi's clone was reportedly standing in as a body double back home. Rival could fly there on its own, so it flew alongside Assistant. As for me, I decided to bring Yuki-chan, Kuro-chan, Fleon-chan and Sage, along with Filolial-sama, who wanted to come too. Filo-tan, apparently, was staying at the castle with Fiancée—Trash's mental state issues were still ongoing, it seemed. The Queen had really wanted to come along regarding unraveling Cal Mira Island's mystery, but given the state of affairs at home, she had to stay behind and mind the fort, it seemed. Éclair, out of sheer stubbornness apparently, decided rebuilding her territory took priority and stayed behind; and since I'd asked Elephant to keep an eye on things, Kou ended up staying with Elephant too. Big Sister and the others likewise decided that village reconstruction took priority over this Cal Mira trip and stayed to prioritize their work there. They said they'd come along later.
And so the ship set sail.
“Bwoo.”
Lazy Pig had tagged along.
“What exactly are you going to Cal Mira Island for, hm?”
“Sounds like Motoyasu-kun's asking Elena-san what SHE's going for... wait, can you even understand her?”
“Not a clue, indeed.”
“Bwoo-boo!”
“Ah, so Elena-san's going on vacation... trying to ride the winning horse, are we?”
“Bwoo!”
Knowing Lazy Pig, it's probably just planning to nap on Cal Mira's beach.
“Bwoo-boo.”

“Huh? You want to negotiate opening a circus on Cal Mira Island? Well... that's not a bad move, actually. It'd liven things up, and a tropical-themed circus might be fun for everyone. Elena-san, you're quite the businesswoman.”
“Bwoo-bwoo-bwoo.”
“'Obviously,' you say? Well... you sure love lecturing me. If anything, you're the one with real business sense here, Elena-san.”
“Lazy Pig has no such talent, I say! If you want to liven things up, get Filolial-sama to sing and dance! There was a loop where we whipped the whole crowd into a frenzy that way!”
It's obviously just angling to laze about. I can see right through it saying pleasant-sounding things!
“Heh... bwoo-bwoo-bwoo.”
Lazy Pig took the chance to mock me something fierce!
“Now, now... anyway, Motoyasu-kun, is it really alright for you to be in usaunny form like that?”
“Ren insisted I stay in this form too, so there was nothing to be done about it, indeed.”

Currently, I was riding the ship in usaunny form. The reason, apparently, was that Ren had to stay in inult form, and it was also useful for cutting down on cabin space aboard the ship. Sure enough, if I turned into a usaunny, the bed could be smaller—plenty of room for sleeping together, too. You'd think Father would do the same, but if Father turned into a peckul, his three slaves might well lose their minds over it, so he only did it when strictly necessary.

And so the ship carried us smoothly to Cal Mira Island. Well, along the way we did run into a storm fierce enough to nearly flip the ship upside down, but that's just a common occurrence for Cal Mira this time of year, indeed. It made me anxious wondering if we'd sink, but mysteriously, we never did. By the way, back in the very first world, we'd have been utterly wrecked with seasickness, but having grown accustomed to the noble brand of queasiness that comes with Filolial-sama, we arrived at the island almost entirely unaffected.
“We've arrived, I say!”

As we disembarked, the ever-familiar lord of the land was there waiting for us. Well, this time around, since Itsuki, Ren, and I were all in our pioneer fairy forms, he stared at us with a startled expression. Naturally, our current state seemed poised to kick the island's vitality into overdrive. He glanced all around, looking rather flustered.
“W-welcome, Four Cardinal Heroes and your parties... at least, that's what I'd normally say, but, um...”

“Er... yes. We already know a fair bit about this island's mystery. Apparently, we heroes have access to a spell that lets us transform into the legendary pioneer fairies, which lets us get closer to unraveling the island's secrets.”
“We did receive word ahead of time from the Melromarc homeland... but seeing it with my own eyes, I'm at a loss for anything but astonishment.”
The count serving as lord of the island let that slip in response to Father's explanation. Well? What did he think of our pretty appearance, hm?
“M-my introduction is overdue. I am Count Havenburg, entrusted with governing these Cal Mira Isles. Pleased to make your acquaintance.”

“Likewise, pleasure to meet you. Er, I'm Naofumi Iwatani, the Shield Hero. This usaunny holding a spear is Motoyasu Kitamura-kun, the Spear Hero, and the one in usaunny form over there is Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero... and—”

As introductions went, among the heroes who'd disembarked, Father turned to face Ren, who had reluctantly come along after being talked into it by Rafumi. Keel and Luna-chan were with him too, by the way.

“I'm Kelsus, the Inult, dog and cooking fairy, woof! Whatever you do, don't mistake me for that busy Sword Hero running all over Melromarc, Ren Amaki, woof! I just happened to come to this island a bit, by some twist of fate, woof!”
So he was keeping up that character, huh.
“So, with that said, please don't press Kelsus-kun about it needlessly.”
“Hey, Sword big bro. Was it really okay for me to come before Raphtalia-chan and the others?”
“I'm not the Sword Hero, woof. Keel, get it through your head already, woof.”
“Fine, got it, big bro Kelsus. Geez, I don't get any of this. Though I do get to eat good food, so—”
Ren was hammering the point home to Keel.
“If I recall, Ren-sama was currently tasked with maintaining public order at home, so we'd asked that he avoid coming to Cal Mira Island...”
“I told you, it's Kelsus, woof! Just ask Rafumi for instructions—she's tagging along anyway, woof! Don't mind me, just go about your business, woof!”
Ren was yapping away like a puppy.
“U-understood.”

The count seemed to accept it, apparently figuring this must be some sort of incognito visit. He kept glancing back and forth between Ren and Keel, by the way. It was obvious at a glance that he thought there were two inults running around.
“Well then, allow me to guide you around the island—”
The count got a distant look in his eyes for some reason, then seemed to think deeply for a moment. And so, as if turning to the group's representative, he addressed Father.
“Ah, are you saying we're short a peckul since there's three fairies here? Wolf!”
“Woof, got it!”
Called by Father, Wolf came over, then unhurriedly cast Fairy Morph and transformed into a peckul.
“Peeen!”
“No... that's not quite it. I was wondering whether it's really alright to have the island tour guided by, well, the very beings said to be the island's legendary native monsters—fairies, was it?”
“Ah, I think I get why that would feel strange. It's probably like teaching Buddha to preach.”
It's the sort of thing where having the very beings from the island's own legends explain the island to you leaves a person with complicated feelings, I say.

“By the way, Father. 'Teaching Buddha to preach' connects to 'teaching Confucius the way of enlightenment.' Though just 'teaching Buddha to preach' gets the meaning across on its own—'the way of enlightenment' means the path of humanity, hop!”
Confucius was a figure famous for the Analects, active in ancient times. There are all sorts of anecdotes about him.

“Confucius was the man who laid the foundations of Confucianism, so lecturing someone like him about the way of enlightenment would be as foolish as a beginner trying to explain things to an expert in the field, hop!”
“There's Motoyasu-kun's trivia for you... though that's a bit that won't land with folks from another world. And you're still using that speech tic, huh?”

By now, there was probably little left in this world that Motoyasu-kun didn't know, and yet he was still so well-versed in things from Japan—Father seemed genuinely impressed. It was a bit embarrassing, I say.
